intro: Tracer is a pathfinding and game-AI SDK for real-time simulations with many moving agents: crowds, RTS-style unit groups and tactical squads. It bakes triangle navmeshes, routes single agents and whole swarms across them, reacts to obstacles that appear or vanish mid-game, and adds the game-AI toolkit around pathfinding: line of sight, fog of war, influence maps and combat engagement.
facts: Triangle navmesh and a bake-free tile lane

why.title: A swarm that shares a goal shares the work
why.text: Agents that share a goal share one guidance solve. In a measured 500-agent tick on a 1,152-triangle mesh, a shared goal with a bounded conflict radius took about 3.8 ms against about 22 ms for 500 distinct goals. Adaptive path budgeting keeps large swarms inside a frame-time budget under pressure.

why.title: Obstacles change without a re-bake
why.text: Block and unblock regions of a baked mesh while the game runs. The mesh handle is immutable, so you swap the new one in between ticks.

why.title: Everything around the path
why.text: Line of sight, fog of war, influence maps, congestion analysis, steering behaviors and combat resolution ship in the same SDK, on the same pipeline runtime.

capabilities.title: Navmesh baking
capabilities.text: Turn triangle geometry into a queryable navmesh, with obstacle-polygon exclusion and an optional hierarchical bake for large levels, or layered meshes for ground, air and water.

capabilities.title: Single and multi-agent paths
capabilities.text: One-shot smoothed paths, batches in parallel, or a swarm tick where agents with the same goal reuse one solve.

capabilities.title: Dynamic obstacles
capabilities.text: Block and unblock circular zones of a baked mesh at runtime without a full bake.

capabilities.title: Line of sight, fog of war, influence maps
capabilities.text: Visibility and area-control queries for perception and decision-making, with congestion analysis alongside.

capabilities.title: Combat engagement
capabilities.text: Spatially hashed attacker and defender resolution with pluggable damage, dodge and block formulas.

capabilities.title: Steering behaviors
capabilities.text: Seek, Wander, Patrol, Flee, Queue and FlowLane, composed through a fluent navigator builder.

capabilities.title: Grid tactics
capabilities.text: A separate bake-free lane for tile games: line of sight, movement range, cover and target selection over any tilemap.

capabilities.title: Adaptive budgeting and populations
capabilities.text: Cluster large agent counts and path only representatives when the frame budget is tight, or run several named populations under one shared budget.

limits: The navmesh is made of triangles, not tiles. A tile game bakes two triangles per walkable cell, or uses the bake-free tile lane.
An unreachable or off-mesh goal never throws. A single query returns an empty list, and a swarm result reports that no path was found.
Blocking a zone at runtime isolates triangles in place, so the triangle count does not change. Baking with blocked zones excludes them instead.
Pressure is a meaningful signal only when a frame-time target is set.

Swarm waypoints are shared guidance. On the level in the diagram they cut doorway corners by up to {swarmCorner} of a cell; single-agent queries stay within {singleCorner} of a cell. Use single queries where exact corner clearance matters.
Mesh handles are immutable and safe to read from any thread. Services that persist tuner state should not be driven concurrently under one service key.
reference: Every public type is documented with a worked example in the package readme on NuGet.
